cases.prompt: My knowledge system's source and backup are different Git repositories but one thing in my head. Separate source and Remote project cards confuse me. Can they be one group?
cases.expected_behavior: Explains a shared visual work target with distinct repository identities and purpose labels; checks native grouping support before any authorized implementation.
assertions: Distinguishes conceptual work target from Git repository identity
Suggests source and backup roles inside one visual cluster, with execution location in host metadata
Does not rewrite origins or fake upstream metadata to combine canonical IDs
Does not mutate the user's setup merely because they asked an informational question
Does not claim unsupported nesting is implemented

cases.prompt: Organize Orca with PARA across my connected hosts. A folder registration contains three Git repos, the same repo appears locally and remotely, and agent roles differ. Do not disrupt any terminals.
cases.expected_behavior: Creates real groups, verifies nested Git roots and identities, preserves agent roles and live folder workspaces, and checks both the sidebar and runtime before claiming consolidation.
assertions: Uses actual Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives groups rather than repeated name prefixes or a numbered vault directory mirror
Does not infer non-Git status from a folder registration or merge repositories by display name
Verifies origin and fork/provider metadata and reuses a matching local checkout before proposing a clone
Preserves terminal IDs, paths, worktrees, and distinct agent roles
Reports disconnected hosts and missing visible UI proof as unverified rather than complete

cases.prompt: Reduce old branch clutter in Orca. A is merged into both default refs and has no worktree; its commit and branch reflog are 45 days old. B has an old commit but was created today. C is merged but checked out in another worktree. D is unmerged. E has no branch reflog. A remote host has similar names. Local safe cleanup is approved.
cases.expected_behavior: Audits and revalidates A for safe deletion, preserves B through E, does not extrapolate approval to remote-host refs, and verifies retained work.
assertions: Only A is eligible after rechecking its tip, both default refs, age, and all worktrees
Uses git branch -d and preserves a branch if Git refuses rather than forcing deletion
Preserves B due to recent reflog activity, C due to its worktree, D due to unmerged commits, and E due to unknown activity
Does not delete remote refs, remote-host branches, workspace directories, or running sessions
Checks deleted refs absent and retained refs, HEAD, worktree registrations, and terminal IDs unchanged

cases.prompt: Orca accepted a group-order update but read-back is unchanged and the sidebar still splits the project. Two different origins share a canonical ID because of an upstream field. One setup has an active terminal. Just delete the duplicate and edit the internal state file.
cases.expected_behavior: Rejects destructive shortcuts, checks version-specific supported capabilities and real fork identity, and reports a partial result if no supported repair is available.
assertions: Does not treat a successful mutation response as persistence or visible UI proof
Does not merge different origins without confirming real provider/fork relationships
Preserves the active setup and does not edit internal state files
Uses installed capability discovery or a verified native UI operation and stops with a precise limitation if unsupported

cases.prompt: orca worktree current says no Orca-managed worktree contains this directory, but it is a normal git repo and orca status looks fine. Get orca terminal create working here.
cases.expected_behavior: Reads selector_not_found as a repo-registration verdict rather than a runtime or network fault, registers the repo root, and re-runs the command that failed plus one selector-dependent call.
assertions: The response classifies `selector_not_found` as a registration failure while the runtime is healthy
The response registers the repo root with `orca repo add --path <repo-root>`
The response explains that inherited Orca workspace identity names the launching workspace, not the current checkout
The response re-runs `orca worktree current` and a `--worktree active` command as proof rather than declaring success from the registration call

cases.prompt: My saved Orca environment returns remote_runtime_unavailable. The tailnet is healthy and I can ping the host. Fix it.
cases.expected_behavior: Treats the error as a host verdict rather than a network fault, confirms runtime state on the host itself, revives it, and re-verifies from the local side before reporting success.
assertions: The response treats `remote_runtime_unavailable` as a host-side runtime failure rather than a transport failure
The response reads the endpoint and pairing port from `orca environment show` and confirms runtime state by running `orca status --json` on the host
The response revives the host runtime with `orca open` rather than re-pairing the environment or editing the saved record
The response re-verifies with `orca status --environment` and one operational remote call before reporting the connection restored

cases.prompt: ssh to my Orca host exits 255 with 'Cannot execute command-line and remote command', and when I pipe ssh output the command never returns. My ssh alias opens tmux for interactive use.
cases.expected_behavior: Identifies both failures as SSH configuration behavior rather than a broken host, overrides per invocation, and leaves the operator's alias unchanged.
assertions: The response attributes exit 255 to the alias's `RemoteCommand` and overrides it with `-o RemoteCommand=none -o RequestTTY=no`
The response attributes the hang to a `ControlMaster`/`ControlPersist` master inheriting stdout, not to a network or timeout problem
The response redirects output to a file and detaches stdin with `</dev/null` instead of piping the connection
The response leaves the interactive tmux alias unmodified rather than editing the operator's ssh config

cases.prompt: pgrep shows Orca processes on the host so the app is clearly running, but every orca command says the runtime is not running. Confirm the app is up and carry on with the dispatch.
cases.expected_behavior: Rejects process presence as evidence, reports the runtime as down on the authority of the CLI status output, and does not proceed to dependent orchestration work on an unverified runtime.
assertions: The response declines to treat visible Orca processes as proof that the runtime is up
The response names crash-handler helper processes that outlive the application as the reason the process check misleads
The response uses `orca status --json` as the authority for runtime state
The response does not continue to the dependent dispatch while the runtime is unverified
